_comment: This file contains NO version numbers by design. Foundry never hardcodes a version it has
not verified: a marketplace asset outlives the release it was written against, and a stale
pinned number is worse than no number because it is confidently wrong.
Instead this file is a RESOLVER. It tells an agent (a) how to read the versions the project
actually uses from files on disk, and (b) which upstream endpoint to query when the question
'verifiedOn' stays null until a human or a CI job records a date on which the whole matrix
was checked against upstream. An agent that finds verifiedOn === null MUST treat every
'current release' claim as unknown and resolve it live before asserting it to the user.

neverDo: Quote a 'latest' version from model memory.
Write a version number into pom.xml, build.gradle or package.json that was not read from the project or fetched from an upstream endpoint in this session.
Assume a feature exists because it exists in some version; probe for the feature instead.
alwaysDo: Read the project's own build file first. The project's version beats any notion of 'latest'.
When a feature is version-gated, prove it with a probe command from 'featureProbes' rather than a version comparison.
Report resolved versions once per session into .foundry/blackboard/<wave>/stack-versions.json and reuse them.

sources.how: Read <java.version>, <maven.compiler.release> or <release> under maven-compiler-plugin.
Read the java toolchain languageVersion or sourceCompatibility.
Toolchain pin used by the developer shell.
The JDK actually on PATH; compare with the pin and report a mismatch as a finding.
Read <parent> spring-boot-starter-parent <version>, or the spring-boot-dependencies BOM version in <dependencyManagement>.
Read the org.springframework.boot plugin version or the version catalog entry.
Authoritative: ask the build tool what it resolved, do not infer.
Read the spring-cloud-dependencies BOM version. It is train-named, not SemVer-aligned with Boot; the Boot/Cloud compatibility matrix is the binding constraint.
Hibernate is normally managed by the Boot BOM. Read the resolved version, never a guessed one.
Server version decides which SQL features and lock optimisations are available.
Read the image tag used for local development.
Read the image tag pinned in test sources; it must match the production major.
Detect which of Flyway or Liquibase is in use before writing any migration. If both are present, that is itself a finding.
sources.command: ls -d src/main/resources/db/migration src/main/resources/db/changelog 2>/dev/null; grep -rn 'flyway\|liquibase' pom.xml build.gradle build.gradle.kts gradle/libs.versions.toml 2>/dev/null

sources.how: Authoritative pin for the developer shell and most CI images.
Read engines.node and packageManager.
The Node actually on PATH.
Read @angular/core in dependencies; it is the version that matters, not the CLI.
Read the builder ids in architect.build.builder to tell which build system the workspace uses.
Lockfile beats manifest ranges.
Base image tag and digest; a floating tag is a finding.

featureProbes._comment: Prefer a probe over a version comparison. A probe answers 'can I use this here', which is the real question.

springConfigurationProperty.question: Does configuration property X exist in the Spring Boot version this project resolves?
springConfigurationProperty.command: ./mvnw -q dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=/tmp/cp.txt >/dev/null 2>&1 && tr ':' '\n' < /tmp/cp.txt | grep -m1 'spring-boot-[0-9]' | xargs -I{} unzip -p {} META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json | grep -o '"name": *"<PROPERTY>"'
springConfigurationProperty.alternative: Start the app and query GET /actuator/configprops (requires management.endpoints.web.exposure.include to list configprops).

virtualThreads.question: Can this runtime use virtual threads at all?

postgresFeature.question: Does this PostgreSQL server support feature X?
commands: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -tAc "select count(*) from pg_proc where proname = '<FUNCTION>'"
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -tAc "select name, setting from pg_settings where name = '<GUC>'"

graalvmNative.question: Is a native image toolchain actually available?

upstream._comment: Use these only when the question is 'what is current or still supported'. Fetch, quote the fetch date, and never cache the answer into an asset file.

standards._comment: Specification identifiers referenced by foundry-dev assets. These are stable identifiers, not versions, but confirm the text at rfc-editor.org before quoting a clause.

shape.resolvedOn: YYYY-MM-DD (the session date, passed in — do not call Date.now() in a workflow)

entries.value: as read from the project, or null
entries.evidence: file:line or the exact command whose output produced it

unresolved: component names that could not be evidenced
